$comment: The x86 sheets' typed opcode table: each line as Intel's opcode tables write it (opcode bytes, /r or /n for ModRM, +rb / +rw / +cc, ib / iw / cb / cw / cp), its Intel assembly, the LLVM X86 records it is (checked by tools/isa/gen-x86.mjs against their opcode, form and immediate), the instruction sets it belongs to, its group, class, description, pseudocode and flags. The generator makes a row per addressing form of a ModRM operand.
